mainTopic: Is a standard נזירות 30 days or 29? The גמרא tests this through רבי אליעזר's rulings and through the dispute of רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן about the פסוק 'עד מלאת הימים'.
overview: Earlier on the daf, רב מתנא holds that a standard נזירות is 30 days, and בר פדא holds it is 29 days. בר פדא supports his view from רבי אליעזר in a משנה: a נזיר who becomes טמא on day 30 loses only seven days, which sounds like his term was already over. The גמרא defends רב מתנא by saying רבי אליעזר holds מקצת היום ככולו, so part of day 30 counts as the whole day. It then challenges this from the next case in that משנה, a 100-day נזיר, where רבי אליעזר says he loses thirty days. ריש לקיש explains that ruling with a פסוק: a נזיר who becomes טמא on the day his term ends gets a standard נזירות. Next the גמרא suggests that רב מתנא and בר פדא follow רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן, who learn the minimum term from different words in the פסוק. רב מתנא answers that both תנאים require thirty days and argue only about whether 'עד' includes the endpoint. Finally, the גמרא explains why רבי יונתן's 'days that need completing' means a month and not a week: a week is never short, but a month can be.

steps.title: בר פדא points to the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא answers רב מתנא's proof by citing the סיפא. There, רבי אליעזר says a נזיר who becomes טמא on day 30 loses only seven days. If a standard נזירות were 30 days, he should lose all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא could answer you: look at the end of the משנה. רבי אליעזר says he loses only seven days. If you think a standard נזירות needs 30 days, he should lose all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: בר פדא pushes back against רב מתנא's proof. He uses the second half of the same משנה to support his own view that a standard נזירות is only 29 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who becomes טמא in the middle of his נזירות loses everything. Someone who becomes טמא after his term is over loses only seven days. רבי אליעזר says the טמא on day 30 loses only seven days, so day 30 must already be after the term, which means the term is 29 days.

keyTerms.meaning: the latter clause (second half) of a משנה
cancels; makes the נזיר lose days he already counted
if it enters your mind; if you were to think
he should cancel all of them

phrases.english: Bar Padda could say to you:
Say the latter clause,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
It cancels only seven days.
If it enters your mind that we require thirty days,
he should cancel all of them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ בַּר פְּדָא: אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב מתנא's proof from the first half of the משנה, which comes before this section.
steps.raayaObject: בר פדא's view that a standard נזירות is 29 days
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר in the סיפא: a נזיר who becomes טמא on day 30 cancels only seven days

steps.title: Part of a day counts as a whole day
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא's view is defended. רבי אליעזר holds מקצת היום ככולו, so once day 30 starts, the 30-day term counts as complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds that part of the day counts like the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב מתנא against בר פדא's proof. רבי אליעזר's ruling does not prove the term is 29 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with a 30-day term, once a little of day 30 has passed, רבי אליעזר treats day 30 as finished. So the טמא on day 30 counts as happening after the term was complete, and that is why he loses only seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds; this is his opinion
part of a day counts like the entire day

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the term is 29 days. The term is still 30 days, but the 30th day counts as finished as soon as it begins.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds:
part of the day is like all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: מִקְצָת הַיּוֹם כְּכוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בר פדא's proof on behalf of רב מתנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives רבי אליעזר's ruling a different reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Losing only seven days proves day 30 is outside the term, so the term is 29 days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The term can still be 30 days, because רבי אליעזר holds part of day 30 counts as the full day.

steps.title: Challenge from the 100-day Nazir
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about a נזיר for 100 days who becomes טמא on day 100 says רבי אליעזר rules he loses thirty days. That fits neither option: with מקצת היום ככולו he should lose seven, and without it he should lose everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if someone says 'I am a נזיר for 100 days' and becomes טמא on day 100, he loses everything. רבי אליעזר says he loses only thirty days. If רבי אליעזר holds part of a day is like the whole day, he should lose seven. If he does not hold that, he should lose everything!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 2. It quotes the next case in the same משנה, a 100-day נזיר, where רבי אליעזר's ruling does not fit the idea of מקצת היום ככולו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both possible ways of understanding רבי אליעזר are tested. If part of day 100 counts as whole, he finished his term and should lose seven. If it does not, he became טמא in the middle and should lose all 100. His answer of thirty matches neither.

keyTerms.meaning: I am hereby a נזיר (the words of the vow)
he became ritually impure

phrases.english: We learned: "I am hereby a nazirite for one hundred days,"
if he became impure on the hundredth day,
it cancels everything.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
It cancels only thirty days.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ סָבַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that Rabbi Eliezer holds
part of the day is like all of it,
he should cancel seven,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא סָבַר מִקְצָת הַיּוֹם כְּכוּלּוֹ —
phrases.english: and if he does not hold part of the day is like all of it,
let him cancel all of them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 2 that רבי אליעזר holds מקצת היום ככולו.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אליעזר holds מקצת היום ככולו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Neither option explains his ruling of thirty days: with the rule he should say seven, and without it he should say all.

steps.title: We do not say part of a day counts as whole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא takes one side: in truth, רבי אליעזר does not hold מקצת היום ככולו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, we do not say that part of the day is like the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer the challenge by choosing one side of the two options. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By dropping מקצת היום ככולו, the גמרא explains why רבי אליעזר does not say seven days in the 100-day case. It still has to explain why he does not say the נזיר loses everything.

keyTerms.meaning: actually; really (the גמרא is settling on one side)
we do not say

phrases.english: Actually, we do not say
part of the day is like all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם לָא אָמְרִינַן מִקְצָת הַיּוֹם כְּכוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks the second option from the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the two options
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר holds מקצת היום ככולו.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר does not hold מקצת היום ככולו.

steps.title: Then he should lose everything
steps.stepSummary: If part of a day does not count as whole, the נזיר became טמא inside his term, so he should lose all the days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should lose all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses the answer of step 4. Without מקצת היום ככולו, why does he not lose all 100 days?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Day 100 is still inside the term, and becoming טמא in the middle of a term normally cancels everything. So why does רבי אליעזר say only thirty?

keyTerms.meaning: if so; if that is the case

phrases.english: If so, let him cancel all of them!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling of thirty days, now that מקצת היום ככולו has been dropped
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Becoming טמא inside the term normally cancels everything, so thirty days needs a reason.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a special rule from the verse
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains רבי אליעזר with a פסוק. A נזיר who becomes טמא on the day his term is completed gets the law of a standard נזיר, so he keeps a standard term of thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: this is רבי אליעזר's reason. The פסוק says, 'This is the law of the נזיר on the day the days of his נזירות are completed.' The תורה is saying: if he became טמא on the day of completion, give him the law of a נזיר, a standard term.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the challenge of step 5. He shows that רבי אליעזר's thirty days comes from a פסוק and not from logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links 'the law of the נזיר' to 'the day of completion.' ריש לקיש reads it as a special rule: becoming טמא on the last day does not cancel everything. Instead, the נזיר must keep one standard נזירות, which is thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: this is the reason
on the day of completion
the law of a נזיר; here, a standard term of נזירות

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר does not hold מקצת היום ככולו. His ruling of thirty days for a נזיר who becomes טמא on his last day comes from the פסוק 'ביום מלאת ימי נזרו,' which gives him a standard נזירות.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ruling of thirty days now rests on a פסוק and no longer on the idea of part of a day. That reopens the question of how רבי אליעזר's ruling in the 30-day case fits רב מתנא's view.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said,
this is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer,
the verse says:
"This is the law of the nazirite,
on the day the days of his naziriteship are complete,"
the Torah said:
if he became impure on the day of completion,
give him the law of a nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learns the rule from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without מקצת היום ככולו, becoming טמא on day 100 should cancel everything.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק sets a special rule: becoming טמא on the day of completion requires one standard term of thirty days.

steps.title: Suggesting a link to the תנאים: רבי יאשיה learns thirty days from hair growth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the dispute matches a dispute of תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי יאשיה learns from 'he shall let his hair grow long' that נזירות cannot be less than thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is like a dispute of תנאים? The פסוק says 'Until the days are complete.' I might think that 'days' means at least two days. So the פסוק says 'He shall be holy, he shall let the locks of his hair grow long.' Hair does not really grow in less than thirty days. These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new move: it suggests that the argument between רב מתנא and בר פדא may be an older argument of תנאים. It begins quoting a ברייתא with רבי יאשיה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'days' alone could mean as little as two days, which would allow a two-day נזירות. רבי יאשיה rejects that reading. He uses the words 'he shall let his hair grow long' to set a minimum, because real hair growth takes thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this is like a dispute between תנאים?
'Until the days are complete' (במדבר 6:5)
The smallest number that 'days' can mean is two
Letting the hair grow long
Therefore the פסוק teaches

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים arrive at thirty, but don't assume yet that they fully agree. In step 9 the גמרא suggests that רבי יונתן's source, a month, could allow twenty-nine days. Only in step 10 does רב מתנא answer that both תנאים require thirty.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is like a dispute of tannaim:
"Until the days are complete",
I would hear that the least amount of "days" is two;
therefore the verse says: "He shall be holy, he shall let the locks grow long,"
and there is no growth of hair in less than thirty days;
these are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי אליעזר discussion and opens a new attempt to connect the רב מתנא / בר פדא dispute to an earlier dispute of תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יאשיה, the minimum נזירות is thirty days, learned from 'he shall let his hair grow long', since hair does not grow in less than thirty days.

steps.title: רבי יונתן learns thirty days from 'until the days are complete'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says the hair-growth proof is not needed. The words 'until the days are complete' already point to a set of days that fill up, which means thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: That is not needed. The פסוק already says 'Until the days are complete.' Which days are days that need to be filled up? You must say: thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי יונתן. He reaches the same thirty days from a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יונתן, the phrase 'until the days are complete' describes a known unit of days that gets 'filled'. That unit is a month, which is full at thirty days. Because he learns from a month, his source may connect to a count shorter than a full thirty, since some months have only twenty-nine days.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (the earlier proof is unnecessary)
To be filled or completed
You must say

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan says: It is not needed,
for it says, "Until the days are complete";

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֵלּוּ הֵן יָמִים שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְמַלּאוֹת?
phrases.english: which are the days that need to be filled up?
You must say: thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the ברייתא: the same thirty days, learned from a different phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יונתן, 'until the days are complete' refers to days that fill up a set unit, a month, so נזירות is thirty days.

steps.title: Proposing that רב מתנא follows רבי יאשיה and בר פדא follows רבי יונתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the two אמוראים are repeating the dispute of the תנאים. רב מתנא follows רבי יאשיה, and בר פדא follows רבי יונתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it so that רב מתנא said his view following רבי יאשיה, and בר פדא said his view following רבי יונתן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its suggestion. It proposes that each אמורא is following a different תנא from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה learns from hair growth, which needs a true thirty days. That fits רב מתנא's thirty-day view. רבי יונתן learns from a month, and a month can be twenty-nine days. That fits בר פדא. If this is right, the argument is not new; it goes back to the תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not so that...? (a suggestion the גמרא is testing)

steps.whatToRemember: This pairing (רב מתנא with רבי יאשיה, בר פדא with רבי יונתן) is only a suggestion. The next step rejects it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'מאי לאו' only offers a suggestion. It is not a final ruling, and the גמרא may still reject it.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו: רַב מַתְנָא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה,
phrases.english: Is it not that Rav Mattana spoke according to Rabbi Yoshiya,
and bar Padda spoke according to Rabbi Yonatan?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו רַב מַתְנָא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from steps 7 and 8 to the dispute between the אמוראים.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute between רב מתנא and בר פדא about the length of a standard נזירות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי יאשיה learns thirty days from hair growth and רבי יונתן learns it from 'until the days are complete'

steps.title: רב מתנא: Everyone agrees on thirty; the argument is about the word 'until'
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא can say that both תנאים require thirty days. They only argue about whether 'עד' includes the last day, and that decides which פסוק each one uses as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנא could answer you: everyone agrees we need thirty days. Here they argue only about whether 'until' includes the endpoint. רבי יאשיה holds 'until' does not include the endpoint. רבי יונתן holds 'until' does include the endpoint.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from the last step that the אמוראים are just repeating the argument of the תנאים. It shows that the תנאים agree on thirty days and argue about something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that נזירות is at least thirty days, so רב מתנא does not have to side with only one of them. Their real argument is about how to read 'עד מלאת הימים'. רבי יאשיה reads 'until' as not including the last day, so these words cannot give him a full thirty, and he needs 'גדל פרע' instead. רבי יונתן reads 'until' as including the last day, so the words themselves already give thirty.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
We require
'Until' and including the endpoint
'Until' but not including the endpoint
They disagree

steps.whatToRemember: The תנאים do not argue about how long נזירות lasts, since both say thirty. They argue about how to read the word 'עד', which changes which פסוק is the source.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יאשיה allows fewer than thirty days. He also requires thirty. He just gets the number from a different פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because the תנאים agree on thirty days, the argument between רב מתנא and בר פדא cannot be pinned onto their argument.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana could say to you:
Everyone agrees that we require thirty days,
and here they disagree about whether "until" means until and including.
phrases.notes: The 'until' is the word in the פסוק 'עד מלאת הימים', 'until the days are complete' (במדבר 6:5).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya holds:
"Until," but not including the endpoint.
And Rabbi Yonatan holds:
"Until," and including the endpoint.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the step 9 proposal that רב מתנא and בר פדא are repeating the argument of the תנאים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the אמוראים' argument matches the argument of רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proposal assumed the תנאים argue about thirty days. In fact both require thirty and argue only about whether 'עד' includes the endpoint.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יונתן's line again: days that need completing means thirty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יונתן's words from the ברייתא again so that it can examine them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Which days are the ones that need to be completed? You must say thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes a line from the ברייתא of רבי יונתן. This is setting up a question about that line, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן says that 'until the days are complete' points to a group of days that sometimes needs to be filled up, and that this is the thirty days of a month. The גמרא brings his words back to check whether this reasoning really leads only to thirty.

keyTerms.meaning: Need to be completed or filled up
You must say

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is רבי יונתן, from the ברייתא quoted earlier.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֵלּוּ הֵן יָמִים שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְמַלּאוֹת
phrases.english: Which are the days that need to be completed?
You must say: thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the comparison between the אמוראים and the תנאים and goes back to examine רבי יונתן's own reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יונתן, 'days that need completing' refers to the thirty days of a month.

steps.title: Challenge: Maybe it means a seven-day week
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why 'days that need completing' could not mean the seven days of a week.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it means a week!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יונתן's reasoning. A week is also a set group of days, so maybe the פסוק means seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'completing the days' just means filling up a fixed group of days, a week also fits that description. That reading would make the shortest נזירות seven days instead of thirty.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead; a way of offering a different reading
Here it means a week of seven days

phrases.english: But say it is a week!
phrases.notes: 'שבת' here means a seven-day week, not the day of שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of רבי יונתן's line quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונתן's claim that 'days that need completing' must mean thirty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A week is also a fixed group of days, so the פסוק could just as easily mean seven.

steps.title: Answer: A week is never short, but a month can be
steps.stepSummary: A week is always seven days, so it never needs to be 'completed'. Only a month, which can be twenty-nine or thirty days, fits that word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The word 'complete' only makes sense for something that can sometimes be short, and a week never is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every week has exactly seven days, so there is nothing to fill up. A month can be twenty-nine days, so the thirtieth day 'completes' it. That is why the פסוק must mean thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there?
A lack; being short

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יונתן, 'until the days are complete' means thirty days because only a month can be short and need completing. A week is always seven days.

phrases.english: With a week, is there ever any lacking?

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any fixed group of days, such as a week, could be called 'days that need completing'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a group that can sometimes be short needs completing. That is a month, so the number is thirty.
